.....Respondents  Date of Institution : 02.05.2023  Arguments heard on: 08.01.2024  Date of Judgment : 14.02.2024 JUDGMENT 1.

Revisionist has filed the present revision petition against impugned order dated 27.01.2023,
passed by Ms. Himanshi Tyagi, Ld. MM-03, East District, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi, whereby application of the revisionist under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. was dismissed.

2. Vide order dated 02.05.2023 passed by my Ld. Predecessor, notice of revision was ordered to be issued only Crl. (R) 113/23 :: 3 ::
against respondent no.1, as the revisionist has failed to satisfy the court as to how other respondents are involved.

Reply has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1.
3.

The factual matrix of the case is that revisionist/ complainant had filed complaint under Section 200 Cr.P.C. against respondents herein and SHO PS Gazipur along with an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. against respondents/ accused persons praying for registration of FIR against them.

The case of the complainant/revisionist is that he had purchased property no. B-272, Gali no.2, Rajbir Colony, Delhi-110096 on 01.05.2018 from Anil Mahto through customary registered sale documents such as GPA, Agreement to Sale, affidavit, receipt, Will and Possession letter.

Anil Mehto handed over earlier chain of documents of the subject property which were executed by recorded owner namely Rishal Singh in favour of Anil Mehato as well as peaceful, physical and vacant possession of the property in question to the complainant.

The complainant got the Arun Kumar vs Shiv Shankar Verma And Ors on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133770764/
2 electricity connection installed in the aforesaid property in the year 2015 and complainant also got three other electricity connections in the said property in the name of his relatives.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Complainant peacefully resided in the property from 2015 to 2019.

Shiv Shankar Verma and his son Lalit Verma (R-1 and R- 2) forged and fabricated documents qua the aforesaid property and got electricity connection in the property on the basis of those forged and fabricated documents in September, 2019 in connivance with officials of BSES.
A complaint was made to SHO, PS Ghazipur against accused Shiv Shanker Verma, Rana Crl.

(R) 113/23 :: 4 ::
Singh and Madhu Singh and officials of BSES on 25.09.2019.
Complainant also made complaint dated 31.08.2021 in the office of BSES regarding changing electricity connection in the property in question but of no avail.
Complainant made complaint dated 23.04.2020 to SHO PS Gazipur against accused persons for extending threats to the complainant and his family members to vacate the suit property.
Accused persons came to the property in question on 25.05.2020 and entered third floor through a tenant of complainant and complaint dated 25.05.2020 was made to SHO PS Ghazipur.

Complainant also made a complaint on 25.07.2021 to SHO PS Ghazipur when accused persons forcibly entered third floor of property of complainant and gave grievous injury to the wife of complainant and FIR under Section 312/21 under Sections 308/323 IPC was registered against accused Neelu Gupta, Lalit Verma,
Rakesh Dedha, Sureshwati and Anita.
However, Police had not registered any case against Shiv Shanker Verma and other accused persons.
Accused persons have no right, title or interest in the property of complainant and they are claiming the same on the basis of forged and fabricated documents.

It is thus, prayed that impugned o r d e r b e s e t a s i d e a n d r e g i s t r a t i o n o f F I R u n d e r s e c t i o n s 467/468/469/471/420/448/452/492/120B/34 IPC be ordered against all the accused persons.
4.

In the present case, ATR was called from concerned Police Station, wherein it is stated that there is property dispute between the parties regarding the property in question and several complaints have been received in PS Gazipur in this regard.

Crl. (R) 113/23 :: 5 ::
Preventive action u/s 107/150 Cr.P.C. has been taken against both the parties.
Even cross-FIRs no. 312/2021 and 313/2021, PS Gazipur are registered against each other and other criminal cases are pending between the parties.
It is stated that matter is civil in nature and required legal and preventive action has already been taken.

5. After hearing Ld. Counsel for the complainant and considering the material available on record, Ld. Trial Court came to the conclusion that identity of accused is known to the complainant and all the facts and circumstances appear to be within knowledge of the complainant and evidence can be conveniently taken without Arun Kumar vs Shiv Shankar Verma And Ors on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133770764/
3 assistance of police investigation.
Further, if there is any need, police inquiry can be held under section 202 Cr.P.C.

sentences.text: Hence, application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. was dismissed.
However, Ld. Trial Court took cognizance of offence of complaint under Section 200 Cr.P.C. and listed the matter for pre-summoning evidence.
6. Ld.
Counsel for the revisionist has submitted that Ld. MM has passed the impugned order dated 27.01.2023 on the basis of surmises and conjectures which is not sustainable in eye of law.
Ld. MM has failed to appreciate that the respondents have forged title documents of the property in question, therefore, police investigation is required in this case.

Offence committed by the respondents is cognizable offence and as per directions of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case Lalita Kumari Vs. Govt. of U.P. & Ors., FIR should be registered against the accused persons/respondents.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Judgment of Ms. Skipper Beverages P. Ltd.
Crl. (R) 113/23 :: 6 ::
vs. State 2002 Crl. LJ NOC 333 (Delhi) does not attract in the present case.
It is thus prayed that impugned order be set aside and registration of FIR against accused persons be ordered.
7. On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for R-1 argued that respondent is owner of the property.
It is revisionist who has forged the documents and claim to be owner of the property in question.

It is argued that claim of revisionist to be owner of the property in question has been rejected before various authorities and when he has failed to establish his claim, he is adopting tactics to involve the respondent and his family members in false criminal cases.
It is argued that there is no infirmity in the impugned order and revision may be dismissed.
8. I have considered the submissions made on behalf of revisionist.
I have also carefully considered the impugned order and other material available on record.

9. Considering the facts of the case in hand, also considering the law laid down in M/S. Skipper Beverages Pvt. Ltd. vs State, 2001 IV AD Delhi 625, I am of the opinion that present dispute between the parties appears to be purely of civil nature.

sentences.text: Even the cross-FIRs no. 312/2021 and 313/2021, PS Gazipur have already been registered against each other and other criminal cases are pending between the parties.
It has rightly been observed by Ld. Trial Court that all the documents and evidence are in custody of the complainant and there is nothing which requires investigation through police.

Ld. Trial Court had further held that if there is any need, police inquiry can be held under section 202 Cr.P.C.
Crl. (R) 113/23 :: 7 ::
10.
Therefore, I am of the opinion that allegations are primarily of civil nature.
Documents and evidences are already in possession of the revisionist.
No detailed investigation is required as the cross-FIRs have already been lodged against each other.
